outputs.L1:
A feeder device configured for mounting on a shelf and for feeding successive products (P) toward a front of the shelf is disclosed. The device comprises an elongated guide member (10) configured to extend longitudinally rearward from the front of the shelf when the device is mounted. A sled (30) is slidably arranged on the guide member (10) such that the sled (30) can slide along the length of the elongated guide member, and is configured to engage a backmost product of the successive products (P) to push the products toward the front of the shelf. The feeder device further comprises means (35) for urging the sled (30) along the guide member (10) toward a front end of the guide member.

Indication means are arranged to indicate that the sled (30) has reached a certain position along the guide member (10). The indication means comprise a transmission member (60), which is longitudinally and limitedly displaceable relative to the guide member (10), and a magnet (37) arranged to connect and disconnect the transmission member (60) with and from the sled (30).
outputs.L2:
A dispensing mechanism adapted to be installed on a shelf advances consecutive products (P) toward the shelf’s front edge. It includes a lengthwise guide element (10) arranged so that, when the mechanism is mounted, it extends rearward from the front of the shelf. A sled (30) is mounted to slide on the guide element (10), allowing it to move along the guide element’s length, and is designed to contact the rearmost item among the successive products (P) so as to drive the products forward.

The mechanism further includes urging means (35) that bias the sled (30) along the guide element (10) toward a front end of the guide element. An indicator arrangement is provided to show when the sled (30) has arrived at a predetermined location along the guide element (10). This indicator arrangement includes a transmission element (60) that can move longitudinally, within a limited range, relative to the guide element (10), and a magnet (37) arranged to couple the transmission element (60) to the sled (30) and to uncouple it from the sled (30).
outputs.L3:
The feeder device is designed to be mounted on a shelf in order to advance a row of products toward the front edge of the shelf. In use, the products are arranged one behind another, and the device ensures that, as products are removed from the front, the remaining products are automatically urged forward so that the next product is presented in an accessible and visible position.

The device includes an elongated guide member that extends rearwardly from the front portion of the shelf. This guide member provides a defined path along which a sled is movable. The sled is supported by the guide member and is arranged to slide back and forth along its length. During operation, the sled is positioned behind the row of products and engages the rearmost product in the row.

When the sled is urged forward, it pushes against the backmost product, thereby advancing the entire row of products toward the front of the shelf. In this way, the device maintains the products in a forward-facing position, improving product presentation and making it easier for a user or customer to remove the foremost product.

A urging mechanism is provided to move the sled along the guide member in a direction toward the front end of the shelf. This mechanism may apply a continuous or intermittent force to the sled so that the sled automatically follows the products as they are removed from the shelf. As a result, the device does not require manual repositioning after each product removal.

The feeder device also includes indication means for signaling when the sled has reached a predetermined position along the guide member. This indication may be used, for example, to show that the product row is nearly empty or that restocking is required. The indication means includes a transmission member that is displaceable only to a limited extent. The transmission member cooperates with a magnet that selectively connects the transmission member to, or disconnects it from, the sled. When the sled reaches the predetermined position, the magnetic connection or disconnection causes the transmission member to actuate or release the indication means, thereby producing a signal corresponding to the position of the sled.

Through this arrangement, the feeder device not only advances products toward the front of a shelf, but also provides a reliable indication of the position of the sled and, consequently, the remaining quantity or status of products on the shelf.
outputs.L4:
A shelf-mounted feeder device is provided for displaying and advancing products on a retail shelf or similar support surface. The device is arranged to move a row of products progressively toward the front edge of the shelf as products are removed by customers. In this way, the foremost product remains presented at or near the shelf front, improving product visibility and accessibility.

The feeder device includes an elongated guide member that extends generally from a rear region of the shelf toward a front region of the shelf. A sled is mounted to the guide member so that it can slide along the length of the guide member. The sled is positioned behind the products carried by the device and acts on the rearmost product in the row. A biasing element, such as a spring or other urging mechanism, urges the sled in a forward direction along the guide member. As the foremost product is removed from the shelf, the sled advances and pushes the remaining products forward.

The device further includes an indication mechanism for determining when the sled has reached a predetermined position along the guide member. This position may correspond, for example, to a low-stock condition, an empty or nearly empty condition, or another selected inventory state. The indication mechanism includes a transmission member that is mounted for limited displacement relative to the guide member or another part of the feeder device. The transmission member is capable of moving only within a restricted range and is not required to travel continuously with the sled along the full length of the guide.

A magnetic coupling is provided between the sled and the transmission member. When the sled is located within a selected region of the guide member, the magnetic coupling connects the sled to the transmission member, allowing movement or position of the sled to be transmitted to the indication mechanism. When the sled moves outside that region, the magnetic coupling is interrupted or disconnected, so that the transmission member is no longer driven by the sled. The magnetic connection may be formed by one or more magnets, magnetically attractable elements, or combinations thereof provided on the sled and the transmission member.

By using a limitedly displaceable transmission member that can be magnetically connected to and disconnected from the sled, the feeder device can provide a reliable indication of the sled reaching a specified position without requiring a mechanical linkage that follows the sled over its entire path of travel. This reduces complexity, limits wear, and allows the indication mechanism to be compactly incorporated into the shelf-mounted feeder device. The indication mechanism may be coupled to a visual indicator, an electrical switch, a sensor, or another signaling component to communicate the detected position of the sled to a user, store employee, or inventory monitoring system.
outputs.L5:
**The Indication**

The indication is often the first sign that something meaningful is about to happen. It may appear as a small detail, a subtle change, or a clear signal that guides attention in a particular direction. In medicine, an indication can explain why a treatment or test is needed. In everyday life, it can be a clue that helps someone make a decision.

The value of an indication depends on how carefully it is observed and understood. A single sign may not always provide a complete answer, but it can lead to further investigation. For example, dark clouds may be an indication of rain, while a sudden drop in energy may be an indication that rest is needed.

In this way, the indication serves as a bridge between uncertainty and understanding. It does not always reveal the full truth immediately, but it points toward what should be considered next. Recognizing the indication at the right time can help prevent mistakes, improve choices, and create better outcomes.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a shelf-mounted product feeder device with an elongated guide rail, a sliding pusher sled, a spring urging the sled forward, and an indicator using a limitedly displaceable transmission member coupled/decoupled to the sled by a magnet.
counterfactuals.output: A shelf-mounted product feeder device includes an elongated guide rail configured to support a row of products and a pusher sled mounted for sliding movement along the guide rail. A spring is operatively connected to the pusher sled to urge the pusher sled in a forward direction for advancing the products toward a front dispensing position. The device further includes an indicator mechanism having a transmission member movable only over a limited displacement range relative to the guide rail. The transmission member is selectively coupled to and decoupled from the pusher sled by a magnetic coupling, such that movement of the pusher sled is transmitted to the indicator during at least a portion of sled travel while permitting relative movement between the sled and the transmission member outside the limited displacement range. The indicator thereby provides a visual or mechanical indication associated with product quantity, sled position, or refill status without requiring the indicator mechanism to travel over the full length of the guide rail.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a formal patent-style description of a feeder device mounted on a shelf for advancing successive products to the shelf front, using reference numerals and including a guide member, slidable sled, forward urging means, and magnetic indication means for detecting a certain sled position.
counterfactuals.output:
A feeder device 10 for presenting products 12 at a front region 14 of a shelf 16 is described. The feeder device 10 is configured to be mounted on, or otherwise supported by, an upper support surface 18 of the shelf 16 and to advance successive products 12 toward the shelf front as leading products are removed.

The feeder device 10 comprises an elongate guide member 20 extending generally in a front-to-rear direction of the shelf 16. The guide member 20 may include a base portion 22 adapted to rest on the shelf 16 and one or more longitudinal guide formations 24, such as rails, ribs, grooves, channels, or tracks. The guide member 20 defines a travel path 26 along which a product-advancing member is movable between a rearward position and a forward position.

A sled 30 is slidably mounted to the guide member 20 for movement along the travel path 26. The sled 30 includes a carriage portion 32 cooperating with the guide formations 24 to maintain the sled 30 in guided alignment during movement. The sled 30 further includes an upstanding pusher wall 34 arranged to engage a rearmost product 12 or a stack of products 12 supported on the shelf 16. In use, the pusher wall 34 urges the products 12 toward the front region 14 of the shelf 16 so that a foremost product is maintained in a display and dispensing position adjacent the shelf front.

Forward urging means 40 is operatively connected between the guide member 20 and the sled 30 to bias the sled 30 toward the front region 14 of the shelf 16. In one embodiment, the forward urging means 40 comprises a coil spring, constant-force spring, elastic member, torsion spring, or other resilient biasing element. The forward urging means 40 may include a spring element 42 having a first end 44 coupled to the guide member 20 and a second end 46 coupled to the sled 30, whereby rearward displacement of the sled 30 stores energy in the spring element 42 and removal of products 12 permits the spring element 42 to drive the sled 30 forward. The forward urging means 40 is selected to apply a force sufficient to advance the products 12 while avoiding excessive compression or damage to the products.

The feeder device 10 further includes magnetic indication means 50 for detecting when the sled 30 reaches, approaches, or occupies a predetermined position along the guide member 20. The magnetic indication means 50 may comprise a magnetic element 52 carried by the sled 30 and a magnetic sensor 54 mounted in a fixed position relative to the guide member 20 or shelf 16. The magnetic element 52 may be a permanent magnet, magnetic strip, ferromagnetic insert, or other magnetically detectable component. The magnetic sensor 54 may comprise a reed switch, Hall-effect sensor, magnetoresistive sensor, or similar detector responsive to the presence, absence, or proximity of the magnetic element 52.

In one arrangement, the magnetic sensor 54 is positioned adjacent a rear portion 56 of the guide member 20 to detect when the sled 30 has been moved to a rearward loading position. In another arrangement, the magnetic sensor 54 is positioned adjacent an intermediate or forward portion 58 of the guide member 20 to detect when the sled 30 has advanced to a low-stock position indicating that a predetermined quantity of products 12 remains on the shelf 16. Upon detection of the magnetic element 52, the magnetic sensor 54 provides an indication signal representative of the position of the sled 30. The indication signal may be supplied to an indicator 60, controller 62, inventory monitoring system, shelf-management system, or remote reporting device.

The magnetic indication means 50 may be arranged such that the magnetic element 52 moves with the sled 30 and passes within a sensing range of the magnetic sensor 54 at the predetermined sled position. Alternatively, the magnetic sensor 54 may be carried by the sled 30 and the magnetic element 52 may be mounted at a fixed location on the guide member 20. In either configuration, the magnetic indication means 50 provides a non-contact indication of the position of the sled 30 without interfering with sliding movement of the sled 30 or product advancement.

During loading, the sled 30 may be manually displaced rearwardly along the guide member 20 against the bias of the forward urging means 40, and products 12 may be placed in front of the pusher wall 34. As products 12 are removed from the front region 14 of the shelf 16, the forward urging means 40 advances the sled 30 and the remaining products 12 forward. When the sled 30 reaches the predetermined position associated with the magnetic indication means 50, the sensor 54 detects the magnetic element 52 and generates the indication signal. The signal may be used to indicate that the feeder device 10 is loaded, depleted, partially depleted, ready for restocking, or otherwise in a selected operational condition.

The guide member 20, sled 30, and associated components may be formed of molded plastics, metals, composite materials, or combinations thereof. The guide member 20 may include mounting features 64, such as adhesive regions, fastener openings, clips, hooks, magnets, or interlocking formations, for securing the feeder device 10 to the shelf 16. The sled 30 may include low-friction surfaces, wheels, runners, or slide pads 66 to reduce resistance during travel. The pusher wall 34 may be planar, curved, perforated, adjustable in height, or otherwise shaped to accommodate different product configurations.

Accordingly, the feeder device 10 provides a shelf-mounted product advancing mechanism in which the sled 30 is guided by the guide member 20 and biased forwardly by the forward urging means 40, while the magnetic indication means 50 detects a selected position of the sled 30 to provide an indication of product inventory or feeder status.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
